newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--There are now fears that the Berisha regime in Albania may turn on the Greek minority in southern Albania as the motivators of the uprising and use them as an excuse for a violent repression.
--Greece has expressed concern that the dramatic developments in Albania could set off a chain reaction in the region.
--Lack of confidence in the market led to panic selling on the Athens bourse despite no changes in Greece's macro-economic indicators and reports that inflation will continue to fall.
--Unionists have rejected a recent proposal that the working week be reduced to 30 hours with a subsequent reduction in pay.

--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos has expressed concern about the security of the ethnic Greek minority in Albania, a possible destabilisation of the entire region and the prospect of a wave of immigrants into Greece.

--Greek businessmen active in Albania are prepared to flee the "now serious" situation in the neighbouring country: Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, has scheduled a Boeing for its Tirana flight today, expecting a rush on seats.

--Athens has sent a strong warning to Tirana to protect the Greek minority in the country. Athens is reportedly prepared to protect Greek lives and property in the event of an escalation of the conflict.
--More than 10,000 hopefuls have applied for just 1,356 seasonal jobs at Greece's national carrier, Olympic Airways.
--The uprising in Albania has provided the Berisha regime with the rationale to move military forces into the south of the country, where the ethnic Greek minority resides.
